Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# COMMAND ALIASES
#
#   Aliases are user commands called with `zk <alias> [<flags>] [<args>]`.
#

#     * you can pipe commands together with the usual | character
#
[alias]
# Here are a few aliases to get you started.

# Shortcut to a command.
#ls = "zk list $@"

# Default flags for an existing command.
#list = "zk list --quiet $@"

# Edit the last modified note.
#editlast = "zk edit --limit 1 --sort modified- $@"

# Edit the notes selected interactively among the notes created the last two weeks.
# This alias doesn't take any argument, so we don't use $@.
#recent = "zk edit --sort created- --created-after 'last two weeks' --interactive"

# Print paths separated with colons for the notes found with the given
# arguments. This can be useful to expand a complex search query into a flag
# taking only paths. For example:
#   zk list --link-to "`zk path -m potatoe`"
#path = "zk list --quiet --format {{path}} --delimiter , $@"

# Show a random note.
#lucky = "zk list --quiet --format full --sort random --limit 1"

# Returns the Git history for the notes found with the given arguments.
# Note the use of a pipe and the location of $@.
#hist = "zk list --format path --delimiter0 --quiet $@ | xargs -t -0 git log --patch --"

# Edit this configuration file.
#conf = '$EDITOR "$ZK_NOTEBOOK_DIR/.zk/config.toml"'

#link-encode-path = true
# Indicates whether a link's path file extension will be removed.
# Defaults to true.
#link-drop-extension = true

colon-tags = false

multiword-tags = false

[tool]

#editor = "vim"

# Pager used to scroll through long output. If you want to disable paging
# altogether, set it to an empty string "".
#pager = "less -FIRX"

# Command used to preview a note during interactive fzf mode.

#fzf-preview = "bat -p --color always {-1}"

[lsp]

[lsp.diagnostics]
# Each diagnostic can have for value: none, hint, info, warning, error

# Report titles of wiki-links as hints.
#wiki-title = "hint"
# Warn for dead links between notes.
dead-link = "error"
# Warn when a note links to itself.
#self-link = "warning"
# Report missing backlinks
#missing-backlink = { level = "hint", position = "bottom" }


[lsp.completion]
# Customize the completion pop-up of your LSP client.

# Show the note title in the completion pop-up, or fallback on its path if empty.
#note-label = "{{title-or-path}}"
# Filter out the completion pop-up using the note title or its path.
#note-filter-text = "{{title}} {{path}}"
# Show the note filename without extension as detail.
#note-detail = "{{filename-stem}}"


# NAMED FILTERS
#

[filter]

# Matches the notes created the last two weeks. For example:

#    $ zk edit recents --interactive
#recents = "--sort created- --created-after 'last two weeks'"

#

# Here are a few aliases to get you started.

# Shortcut to a command.
#ls = "zk list $@"

# Default flags for an existing command.
#list = "zk list --quiet $@"

# Edit the last modified note.
#editlast = "zk edit --limit 1 --sort modified- $@"

# Edit the notes selected interactively among the notes created the last two weeks.
# This alias doesn't take any argument, so we don't use $@.

def eprint(s):
    sys.stderr.write(s + "\n")

def error_exit(msg):
    eprint(f"zk: error: {msg}")
    sys.exit(1)

def parse_global_flags(argv):
    # returns dict with notebook_dir, working_dir, no_input, help, remaining, error
    notebook_dir = None
    working_dir = None
    no_input = False
    help_flag = False
    remaining = []
    i=0
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if a in ("-h","--help"):
            help_flag=True
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
        elif a == "--notebook-dir":
            if i+1 >= len(argv):
                error_exit('expected value for --notebook-dir')
            notebook_dir = argv[i+1]
            i+=2
        elif a.startswith("--notebook-dir="):
            notebook_dir = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a in ("-W","--working-dir"):
            if i+1 >= len(argv):
                error_exit('expected value for --working-dir')
            working_dir = argv[i+1]
            i+=2
        elif a.startswith("-W="):
            working_dir = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a.startswith("--working-dir="):
            working_dir = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a == "--no-input":
            no_input=True
            i+=1
        elif a == "--":
            remaining.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        elif a.startswith("-") and a not in ("-h","--help","-W","--working-dir","--notebook-dir","--no-input"):
            # unknown global flag? For top-level we need to handle suggestion
            # if we are at global parsing before command, unknown flag should be reported.
            # Keep as remaining for command handling? But for top-level unknown we should error now.
            # We can detect if no command yet and flag looks like -Z
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
        else:
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
    return notebook_dir, working_dir, no_input, help_flag, remaining

def find_notebook(start_dir, notebook_dir_override):
    if notebook_dir_override:
        # resolve relative to start_dir if needed
        if not os.path.isabs(notebook_dir_override):
            cand = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(start_dir, notebook_dir_override))
        else:
            cand = os.path.abspath(notebook_dir_override)
        # check existence; if not exists, warn twice and fail
        if not os.path.exists(cand):
            eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
            eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
            error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cand} or a parent directory")
        # check .zk
        zk_path = os.path.join(cand, ".zk")
        if os.path.isdir(zk_path):
            return cand
        # walk up from cand
        cur = cand
        while True:
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(cur, ".zk")):
                return cur
            parent = os.path.dirname(cur)
            if parent == cur:
                break
            cur = parent
        eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
        eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
        error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cand} or a parent directory")
        return None
    else:
        cur = os.path.abspath(start_dir)
        while True:
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(cur, ".zk")):
                return cur
            parent = os.path.dirname(cur)
            if parent == cur:
                break
            cur = parent
        error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {os.path.abspath(start_dir)} or a parent directory")

    config_path = os.path.join(notebook_dir, ".zk", "config.toml")
    defaults = {
        "note": {
            "filename": "{{id}}",
            "extension": "md",
            "template": "default.md",

            "id-charset": "alphanum",

                "hashtags": True,
                "colon-tags": False,
                "multiword-tags": False,
            }
        },
        "extra": {},
        "tool": {},
    }
    # try tomli
    try:
        # Python 3.11 has tomllib, else try tomli
        try:
            import tomllib
            with open(config_path, "rb") as f:
                data = tomllib.load(f)
        except ImportError:
            import tomli
            with open(config_path, "rb") as f:
                data = tomli.load(f)
        except Exception:
            data = {}
        # merge simple keys
        if data:
            # deep update
            def deep_update(dst, src):
                for k,v in src.items():
                    if isinstance(v, dict) and k in dst and isinstance(dst[k], dict):
                        deep_update(dst[k], v)
                    else:
                        dst[k]=v
            deep_update(defaults, data)
    except Exception:
        pass
    # also parse via fallback regex if tomli not available? Already attempted
    return defaults

def parse_frontmatter(raw):
    metadata={}
    content=raw
    if raw.startswith("---\n") or raw.startswith("---\r\n"):
        lines=raw.splitlines()
        if len(lines)>=2 and lines[0].strip()=="---":
            end_idx=-1
            for idx in range(1,len(lines)):
                if lines[idx].strip()=="---":
                    end_idx=idx
                    break
            if end_idx!=-1:
                fm_lines=lines[1:end_idx]
                # simple parse
                for line in fm_lines:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                        continue
                    if ":" not in line:
                        continue
                    key, val = line.split(":",1)
                    key=key.strip()
                    val=val.strip()
                    if val.startswith("[") and val.endswith("]"):
                        inner=val[1:-1].strip()
                        if not inner:
                            arr=[]
                        else:
                            # split by comma not inside quotes simple
                            parts=[p.strip() for p in inner.split(",")]
                            arr=[]
                            for p in parts:
                                p=p.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
                                if p:
                                    arr.append(p)
                            val=arr
                    elif (val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"')) or (val.startswith("'") and val.endswith("'")):
                        val=val[1:-1]
                    # try to keep as string
                    metadata[key]=val
                # content after frontmatter
                content="\n".join(lines[end_idx+1:])
                # remove leading newline
                if content.startswith("\n"):
                    content=content[1:]
                # But rawContent remains original
                # For body parsing we use content without frontmatter
                pass
    return metadata, content

def extract_title(metadata, content_without_fm, raw):
    if "title" in metadata and isinstance(metadata["title"], str) and metadata["title"].strip():
        return metadata["title"].strip()
    # find first markdown heading
    for line in content_without_fm.splitlines():
        m=re.match(r'^\s*#\s+(.*)', line)
        if m:
            t=m.group(1).strip()
            # remove possible closing #?
            t=re.sub(r'\s+#+\s*$','',t)
            return t
    return ""

def extract_tags(metadata, body, text_for_hashtags, config):
    tags=[]
    # from metadata tags
    if "tags" in metadata:
        val=metadata["tags"]
        if isinstance(val, list):
            tags.extend(val)
        elif isinstance(val, str):
            # split by comma?
            if "," in val:
                tags.extend([p.strip() for p in val.split(",") if p.strip()])
            else:
                tags.extend([p.strip() for p in val.split() if p.strip()])
    # hashtags
    hashtags_enabled = config.get("format",{}).get("markdown",{}).get("hashtags", True)
    if hashtags_enabled:
        # simple regex #word
        # Use same as observed: hashtags are # followed by alphanum _ -
        # Avoid matching "##" etc
        # find all #tag
        # The body may contain #mytag
        # Also handle that hashtags may be at start?
        # Use regex
        pattern=r'(?:^|[\s])#([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)'
        for m in re.finditer(pattern, text_for_hashtags):
            tag=m.group(1)
            if tag:
                tags.append(tag)
        # Also multiword? ignore
        # colon-tags: pattern :tag: if enabled? ignore for now if disabled
        colon_enabled = config.get("format",{}).get("markdown",{}).get("colon-tags", False)
        if colon_enabled:
            for m in re.finditer(r':([A-Za-z0-9_\-:]+):', text_for_hashtags):
                tag=m.group(1)
                if tag:
                    # colon tags may contain colons; but simple
                    tags.append(tag)
    # deduplicate preserve order? We'll keep as seen order, unique
    seen=set()
    uniq=[]
    for t in tags:
        if t not in seen:
            seen.add(t)
            uniq.append(t)
    return uniq

def parse_links_and_snippets(raw, body, paragraphs):
    # raw is full rawContent, body is body without heading etc.
    # paragraphs is list of paragraph strings (from body)
    links=[]
    # need to map paragraph to offset in raw
    # compute offset for each paragraph by finding in raw
    # For snippet start/end, use raw.find(paragraph)
    # But paragraphs may have been trimmed; raw.find may not exact due to newline differences.
    # Alternative: find paragraph start by searching raw.
    for para in paragraphs:
        if not para.strip():
            continue
        # find links in para
        # wiki links
        for m in re.finditer(r'\[\[([^\]]+)\]\]', para):
            inner=m.group(1)
            # split by | or #?
            href=inner.split("|")[0].split("#")[0].strip()
            title=inner.strip()
            # Determine if contains | then title after |
            if "|" in inner:
                parts=inner.split("|",1)
                href=parts[0].strip()
                title=parts[1].strip()
            # snippet is para text stripped? but preserve as in DB: snippet equals paragraph text (with links)
            snippet=para.strip()
            # compute snippetStart/End
            # find snippet in raw
            try:
                start=raw.index(snippet)
            except:
                # try stripped para find in body?
                try:
                    start=raw.index(para)
                except:
                    start=0
            end=start+len(snippet)
            links.append({
                "href": href,
                "title": title,
                "snippet": snippet,
                "snippet_start": start,
                "snippet_end": end,
                "type": "wiki-link",
                "external": 0,
            })
        # markdown links
        for m in re.finditer(r'\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]+)\)', para):
            text=m.group(1)
            href=m.group(2).strip()
            title=text if text else href
            snippet=para.strip()
            try:
                start=raw.index(snippet)
            except:
                try:
                    start=raw.index(para)
                except:
                    start=0
            end=start+len(snippet)
            # external?
            external=1 if href.startswith("http://") or href.startswith("https://") or href.startswith("mailto:") else 0
            links.append({
                "href": href,
                "title": title,
                "snippet": snippet,
                "snippet_start": start,
                "snippet_end": end,
                "type": "markdown",
                "external": external,
            })
    return links

def parse_note_file(notebook_dir, rel_path, config):
    abs_path=os.path.join(notebook_dir, rel_path)
    raw=open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
    checksum=hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    metadata, content_without_fm = parse_frontmatter(raw)
    title=extract_title(metadata, content_without_fm, raw)
    # Determine body: after removing frontmatter, remove first heading line if present
    body_content=content_without_fm
    # remove leading title heading line
    lines=body_content.splitlines()
    idx=0
    # skip leading empty lines
    while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx].strip()=="":
        idx+=1
    if idx < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*#\s+', lines[idx]):
        # remove that line
        idx+=1
        # also skip following blank line(s)
        while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx].strip()=="":
            idx+=1
    body="\n".join(lines[idx:]).strip()
    # But we need preserve original paragraphs for lead/snippets?
    # For lead: first paragraph of body (split by \n\n)
    if body:
        # split paragraphs by blank line
        paras=[p.strip() for p in re.split(r'\n\s*\n', body) if p.strip()!='']
        lead=paras[0] if paras else ""
        # Need to clean lead from markdown? Keep as is? For def2 lead included #mytag etc as raw
        # We'll keep as is but need to decide: lead should be plain text maybe without extra?
        # Observed lead for def2 is "This is a note with #mytag and a link [[abc1]]." which matches first paragraph exactly.
        # paragraphs list for body is same paras but with original newlines? Use paras as above
    else:
        paras=[]
        lead=""
    # tags extraction: use text_for_hashtags = body + maybe title? But earlier tags from body only, not title. Use body?
    # For completeness, also search raw? But tags in body only; we search body+content_without_fm
    text_for_hashtags=body
    tags=extract_tags(metadata, body, text_for_hashtags, config)
    # wordCount as whitespace split of raw
    word_count=len(raw.split())

def render_template(template_str, context):
    # Very simple handlebars-like
    # Supports {{var}}, {{extra.key}}, {{slug title}}, {{format-date now}}, {{format-date now "format"}}, {{filename}}, etc
    # We'll implement via regex
    def slugify(text):
        text=text.lower()
        # replace non alnum with -
        text=re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+','-',text)
        text=text.strip("-")
        return text
    def format_date(val, fmt=None):
        # val may be datetime or string "now"
        if isinstance(val, str) and val=="now":
            dt=datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        elif isinstance(val, datetime.datetime):
            dt=val
        else:
            # try parse string date
            try:
                dt=datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(val.replace("Z","+00:00"))
            except:
                dt=datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        if fmt is None:
            return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        # handle go-like format? Original uses "%Y-%m-%d" style when passed via template like "{{format-date now \"%Y-%m-%d\"}}"
        # fmt string may include %Y etc
        try:
            return dt.strftime(fmt)
        except:
            return dt.isoformat()
    # Need to handle now variable: context may have 'now' datetime
    # Handle each {{...}}
    pattern=re.compile(r'{{\s*(.*?)\s*}}')
    def repl(m):
        expr=m.group(1).strip()
        # handle slug
        if expr.startswith("slug "):
            arg=expr[5:].strip()
            val=context.get(arg, "")
            return slugify(str(val))
        elif expr.startswith("format-date"):
            # format-date <val> [<format>]
            # Parse: format-date now "%Y-%m-%d"  or format-date now
            inner=expr[len("format-date"):].strip()
            # split respecting quotes
            parts=re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"|\'([^\']*)\'|(\S+)', inner)
            tokens=[]
            for a,b,c in parts:
                if a:
                    tokens.append(a)
                elif b:
                    tokens.append(b)
                elif c:
                    tokens.append(c)
            if not tokens:
                return ""
            val_token=tokens[0]
            # resolve val_token from context or literal
            if val_token=="now":
                val="now"
            else:
                val=context.get(val_token, val_token)
            fmt=tokens[1] if len(tokens)>1 else None
            return format_date(val, fmt)
        elif expr.startswith("json "):
            # {{json .}}
            var=expr[5:].strip()
            # return json of context?
            return json.dumps(context)
        elif "." in expr:
            # e.g., extra.key or title-or-path etc.
            parts=expr.split(".",1)
            base=parts[0]
            rest=parts[1]
            if base=="extra":
                return str(context.get("extra",{}).get(rest,""))
            elif base=="metadata":
                return str(context.get("metadata",{}).get(rest,""))
            else:
                # unknown
                return ""
        else:
            # simple var
            # also handle title-or-path etc? Not needed
            if expr=="title-or-path":
                return context.get("title") or context.get("path") or ""
            if expr=="filename-stem":
                return context.get("filenameStem","")
            if expr=="now":
                # as per earlier test, {{now}} prints something like "2026-09-06 14:46:04.39897495 +0000 UTC m=+0.015449561"
                # Provide similar
                return datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f +0000 UTC")
            return str(context.get(expr,""))
    return pattern.sub(repl, template_str)

def load_template_file(notebook_dir, template_path):
    # template_path may be relative to .zk/templates or absolute or ~/...
    if os.path.isabs(template_path) or template_path.startswith("~/"):
        expanded=os.path.expanduser(template_path)
        if os.path.exists(expanded):
            return open(expanded, "r", encoding="utf-8").read()
        else:
            return None
    # relative to .zk/templates
    cand=os.path.join(notebook_dir, ".zk", "templates", template_path)
    if os.path.exists(cand):
        return open(cand, "r", encoding="utf-8").read()
    # also try relative to notebook_dir?
    cand2=os.path.join(notebook_dir, template_path)
    if os.path.exists(cand2):
        return open(cand2, "r", encoding="utf-8").read()
    return None

def eprint(s):
    sys.stderr.write(s + "\n")

def error_exit(msg):
    eprint(f"zk: error: {msg}")
    sys.exit(1)

def parse_global_flags(argv):
    # returns dict with notebook_dir, working_dir, no_input, help, remaining, error
    notebook_dir = None
    working_dir = None
    no_input = False
    help_flag = False
    remaining = []
    i=0
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if a in ("-h","--help"):
            help_flag=True
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
        elif a == "--notebook-dir":
            if i+1 >= len(argv):
                error_exit('expected value for --notebook-dir')
            notebook_dir = argv[i+1]
            i+=2
        elif a.startswith("--notebook-dir="):
            notebook_dir = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a in ("-W","--working-dir"):
            if i+1 >= len(argv):
                error_exit('expected value for --working-dir')
            working_dir = argv[i+1]
            i+=2
        elif a.startswith("-W="):
            working_dir = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a.startswith("--working-dir="):
            working_dir = a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a == "--no-input":
            no_input=True
            i+=1
        elif a == "--":
            remaining.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        elif a.startswith("-") and a not in ("-h","--help","-W","--working-dir","--notebook-dir","--no-input"):
            # unknown global flag? For top-level we need to handle suggestion
            # if we are at global parsing before command, unknown flag should be reported.
            # Keep as remaining for command handling? But for top-level unknown we should error now.
            # We can detect if no command yet and flag looks like -Z
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
        else:
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
    return notebook_dir, working_dir, no_input, help_flag, remaining

def find_notebook(start_dir, notebook_dir_override):
    if notebook_dir_override:
        # resolve relative to start_dir if needed
        if not os.path.isabs(notebook_dir_override):
            cand = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(start_dir, notebook_dir_override))
        else:
            cand = os.path.abspath(notebook_dir_override)
        # check existence; if not exists, warn twice and fail
        if not os.path.exists(cand):
            eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
            eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
            error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cand} or a parent directory")
        # check .zk
        zk_path = os.path.join(cand, ".zk")
        if os.path.isdir(zk_path):
            return cand
        # walk up from cand
        cur = cand
        while True:
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(cur, ".zk")):
                return cur
            parent = os.path.dirname(cur)
            if parent == cur:
                break
            cur = parent
        eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
        eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
        error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cand} or a parent directory")
        return None
    else:
        cur = os.path.abspath(start_dir)
        while True:
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(cur, ".zk")):
                return cur
            parent = os.path.dirname(cur)
            if parent == cur:
                break
            cur = parent
        error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {os.path.abspath(start_dir)} or a parent directory")

            def deep_update(dst, src):
                for k,v in src.items():
                    if isinstance(v, dict) and k in dst and isinstance(dst[k], dict):
                        deep_update(dst[k], v)
                    else:
                        dst[k]=v
            deep_update(defaults, data)
    except Exception:
        pass
    # also parse via fallback regex if tomli not available? Already attempted
    return defaults

def parse_frontmatter(raw):
    metadata={}
    content=raw
    if raw.startswith("---\n") or raw.startswith("---\r\n"):
        lines=raw.splitlines()
        if len(lines)>=2 and lines[0].strip()=="---":
            end_idx=-1
            for idx in range(1,len(lines)):
                if lines[idx].strip()=="---":
                    end_idx=idx
                    break
            if end_idx!=-1:
                fm_lines=lines[1:end_idx]
                # simple parse
                for line in fm_lines:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                        continue
                    if ":" not in line:
                        continue
                    key, val = line.split(":",1)
                    key=key.strip()
                    val=val.strip()
                    if val.startswith("[") and val.endswith("]"):
                        inner=val[1:-1].strip()
                        if not inner:
                            arr=[]
                        else:
                            # split by comma not inside quotes simple
                            parts=[p.strip() for p in inner.split(",")]
                            arr=[]
                            for p in parts:
                                p=p.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
                                if p:
                                    arr.append(p)
                            val=arr
                    elif (val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"')) or (val.startswith("'") and val.endswith("'")):
                        val=val[1:-1]
                    # try to keep as string
                    metadata[key]=val
                # content after frontmatter
                content="\n".join(lines[end_idx+1:])
                # remove leading newline
                if content.startswith("\n"):
                    content=content[1:]
                # But rawContent remains original
                # For body parsing we use content without frontmatter
                pass
    return metadata, content

def extract_title(metadata, content_without_fm, raw):
    if "title" in metadata and isinstance(metadata["title"], str) and metadata["title"].strip():
        return metadata["title"].strip()
    # find first markdown heading
    for line in content_without_fm.splitlines():
        m=re.match(r'^\s*#\s+(.*)', line)
        if m:
            t=m.group(1).strip()
            # remove possible closing #?
            t=re.sub(r'\s+#+\s*$','',t)
            return t
    return ""

def extract_tags(metadata, body, text_for_hashtags, config):
    tags=[]
    # from metadata tags
    if "tags" in metadata:
        val=metadata["tags"]
        if isinstance(val, list):
            tags.extend(val)
        elif isinstance(val, str):
            # split by comma?
            if "," in val:
                tags.extend([p.strip() for p in val.split(",") if p.strip()])
            else:
                tags.extend([p.strip() for p in val.split() if p.strip()])
    # hashtags
    hashtags_enabled = config.get("format",{}).get("markdown",{}).get("hashtags", True)
    if hashtags_enabled:
        # simple regex #word
        # Use same as observed: hashtags are # followed by alphanum _ -
        # Avoid matching "##" etc
        # find all #tag
        # The body may contain #mytag
        # Also handle that hashtags may be at start?
        # Use regex
        pattern=r'(?:^|[\s])#([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)'
        for m in re.finditer(pattern, text_for_hashtags):
            tag=m.group(1)
            if tag:
                tags.append(tag)
        # Also multiword? ignore
        # colon-tags: pattern :tag: if enabled? ignore for now if disabled
        colon_enabled = config.get("format",{}).get("markdown",{}).get("colon-tags", False)
        if colon_enabled:
            for m in re.finditer(r':([A-Za-z0-9_\-:]+):', text_for_hashtags):
                tag=m.group(1)
                if tag:
                    # colon tags may contain colons; but simple
                    tags.append(tag)
    # deduplicate preserve order? We'll keep as seen order, unique
    seen=set()
    uniq=[]
    for t in tags:
        if t not in seen:
            seen.add(t)
            uniq.append(t)
    return uniq

def parse_links_and_snippets(raw, body, paragraphs):
    # raw is full rawContent, body is body without heading etc.
    # paragraphs is list of paragraph strings (from body)
    links=[]
    # need to map paragraph to offset in raw
    # compute offset for each paragraph by finding in raw
    # For snippet start/end, use raw.find(paragraph)
    # But paragraphs may have been trimmed; raw.find may not exact due to newline differences.
    # Alternative: find paragraph start by searching raw.
    for para in paragraphs:
        if not para.strip():
            continue
        # find links in para
        # wiki links
        for m in re.finditer(r'\[\[([^\]]+)\]\]', para):
            inner=m.group(1)
            # split by | or #?
            href=inner.split("|")[0].split("#")[0].strip()
            title=inner.strip()
            # Determine if contains | then title after |
            if "|" in inner:
                parts=inner.split("|",1)
                href=parts[0].strip()
                title=parts[1].strip()
            # snippet is para text stripped? but preserve as in DB: snippet equals paragraph text (with links)
            snippet=para.strip()
            # compute snippetStart/End
            # find snippet in raw
            try:
                start=raw.index(snippet)
            except:
                # try stripped para find in body?
                try:
                    start=raw.index(para)
                except:
                    start=0
            end=start+len(snippet)
            links.append({
                "href": href,
                "title": title,
                "snippet": snippet,
                "snippet_start": start,
                "snippet_end": end,
                "type": "wiki-link",
                "external": 0,
            })
        # markdown links
        for m in re.finditer(r'\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]+)\)', para):
            text=m.group(1)
            href=m.group(2).strip()
            title=text if text else href
            snippet=para.strip()
            try:
                start=raw.index(snippet)
            except:
                try:
                    start=raw.index(para)
                except:
                    start=0
            end=start+len(snippet)
            # external?
            external=1 if href.startswith("http://") or href.startswith("https://") or href.startswith("mailto:") else 0
            links.append({
                "href": href,
                "title": title,
                "snippet": snippet,
                "snippet_start": start,
                "snippet_end": end,
                "type": "markdown",
                "external": external,
            })
    return links

def parse_note_file(notebook_dir, rel_path, config):
    abs_path=os.path.join(notebook_dir, rel_path)
    raw=open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
    checksum=hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    metadata, content_without_fm = parse_frontmatter(raw)
    title=extract_title(metadata, content_without_fm, raw)
    # Determine body: after removing frontmatter, remove first heading line if present
    body_content=content_without_fm
    # remove leading title heading line
    lines=body_content.splitlines()
    idx=0
    # skip leading empty lines
    while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx].strip()=="":
        idx+=1
    if idx < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*#\s+', lines[idx]):
        # remove that line
        idx+=1
        # also skip following blank line(s)
        while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx].strip()=="":
            idx+=1
    body="\n".join(lines[idx:]).strip()
    # But we need preserve original paragraphs for lead/snippets?
    # For lead: first paragraph of body (split by \n\n)
    if body:
        # split paragraphs by blank line
        paras=[p.strip() for p in re.split(r'\n\s*\n', body) if p.strip()!='']
        lead=paras[0] if paras else ""
        # Need to clean lead from markdown? Keep as is? For def2 lead included #mytag etc as raw
        # We'll keep as is but need to decide: lead should be plain text maybe without extra?
        # Observed lead for def2 is "This is a note with #mytag and a link [[abc1]]." which matches first paragraph exactly.
        # paragraphs list for body is same paras but with original newlines? Use paras as above
    else:
        paras=[]
        lead=""
    # tags extraction: use text_for_hashtags = body + maybe title? But earlier tags from body only, not title. Use body?
    # For completeness, also search raw? But tags in body only; we search body+content_without_fm
    text_for_hashtags=body
    tags=extract_tags(metadata, body, text_for_hashtags, config)
    # wordCount as whitespace split of raw
    word_count=len(raw.split())
    # links
    links=parse_links_and_snippets(raw, body, paras)
    # snippet list: if lead exists, snippets=[lead]
    snippets=[lead] if lead else []
    # metadata json
    # filename
    filename=os.path.basename(rel_path)
    filenameStem=os.path.splitext(filename)[0]
    return {
        "path": rel_path,
        "sortable_path": rel_path,
        "filename": filename,
        "filenameStem": filenameStem,
        "title": title,
        "lead": lead,
        "body": body,
        "raw_content": raw,
        "word_count": word_count,
        "checksum": checksum,
        "metadata": metadata,
        "tags": tags,
        "links": links,
        "snippets": snippets,
        "paras": paras,
    }

def index_notebook(notebook_dir, verbose=False, quiet=False, force=False):
    config=load_config(notebook_dir)
    exclude_patterns=config.get("note",{}).get("exclude", [])
    if exclude_patterns is None:
        exclude_patterns=[]
    extension=config.get("note",{}).get("extension","md")
    db_path=os.path.join(notebook_dir, ".zk", "notebook.db")
    conn=sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    cur=conn.cursor()
    # ensure metadata exists?
    # scan files
    all_notes=[]
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(notebook_dir):
        # skip .zk
        if ".zk" in dirs:
            dirs.remove(".zk")
        # also skip hidden? Not needed
        # check root is within notebook
        rel_root=os.path.relpath(root, notebook_dir)
        if rel_root==".":
            rel_root=""
        # check exclude patterns for directories?
        # For each dir, maybe skip if matches exclude?
        # Exclude handling: path globs ignored while indexing
        # Use fnmatch
        # If exclude pattern matches directory path, prune
        # For simplicity, skip processing if rel_root matches exclude
        # We'll handle later per file
        for fname in files:
            if not fname.endswith("."+extension):
                continue
            abs_path=os.path.join(root, fname)
            rel_path=os.path.join(rel_root, fname) if rel_root else fname
            rel_path=rel_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
            # check exclude globs
            excluded=False
            for pat in exclude_patterns:
                # glob match using fnmatch
                if fnmatch.fnmatch(rel_path, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(fname, pat):
                    excluded=True
                    break
            if excluded:
                continue
            all_notes.append(rel_path)
    # fetch existing notes from DB
    cur.execute("SELECT id, path, checksum, created, modified FROM notes")
    existing={row[1]: (row[0], row[2], row[3], row[4]) for row in cur.fetchall()}
    # stats
    added=0
    modified_cnt=0
    removed=0
    # process each found file

    for rel_path in all_notes:
        seen.add(rel_path)

        checksum=parsed["checksum"]
        if rel_path in existing:
            nid, old_checksum, old_created, old_modified = existing[rel_path]
            if not force and checksum==old_checksum:
                # unchanged, but still need to update FTS? Not needed
                if verbose:
                    # will print later?
                    pass
                continue
            else:
                # modified
                # update note
                # Keep created, update modified to file mtime
                stat=os.stat(abs_path)
                mtime=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00","Z")
                # But original stores with +00:00? In DB they store with +00:00; JSON shows Z.
                # We'll store DB with format like 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff+00:00'
                # For consistency, store as ISO with +00:00
                db_modified=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f+00:00")
                # But preserve microsecond nanosecond? We'll use st_mtime ns for nanosecond?
                # Use stat.st_mtime_ns if available
                try:
                    ns=stat.st_mtime_ns
                    sec=ns//1_000_000_000
                    nsec=ns%1_000_000_000
                    dt=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(sec, tz=timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=nsec//1000)
                    # Need nanosecond precision 9 digits, but we can fake as microsecond*1000

                    db_modified=f"{dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}.{nsec:09d}+00:00"

                # update notes
                cur.execute("UPDATE notes SET title=?, lead=?, body=?, raw_content=?, word_count=?, checksum=?, modified=?, metadata=?, filename=?, sortable_path=? WHERE id=?",
                    (parsed["title"], parsed["lead"], parsed["body"], parsed["raw_content"], parsed["word_count"], checksum, db_modified, json.dumps(parsed["metadata"]), parsed["filename"], parsed["sortable_path"], nid))

            # end modified
        else:

            stat=os.stat(abs_path)
            try:

                sec=ns//1_000_000_000
                nsec=ns%1_000_000_000
                dt=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(sec, tz=timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=nsec//1000)
                base=dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

                now_nsec=now_ns%1_000_000_000
                now_dt=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(now_sec, tz=timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=now_nsec//1000)
                base2=now_dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
                db_created=f"{base2}.{now_nsec:09d}+00:00"
            except:
                now=datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

                db_modified=now
            cur.execute("INSERT INTO notes (path, sortable_path, title, lead, body, raw_content, word_count, checksum, created, modified, metadata, filename) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                (parsed["path"], parsed["sortable_path"], parsed["title"], parsed["lead"], parsed["body"], parsed["raw_content"], parsed["word_count"], checksum, db_created, db_modified, json.dumps(parsed["metadata"]), parsed["filename"]))
            nid=cur.lastrowid
            # FTS
            try:
                cur.execute("INSERT INTO notes_fts(rowid, path, title, body) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", (nid, parsed["path"], parsed["title"], parsed["body"]))
            except:
                pass
            existing[rel_path]=(nid, checksum, db_created, db_modified)
            added+=1
        # we will handle tags and links after loop for all?
    # Handle deletions: notes in DB but not seen
    for path, (nid, _, _, _) in list(existing.items()):
        if path not in seen:
            # ensure path was originally from DB but now missing
            # Check if file still exists but was excluded? Already not in seen
            # Delete

            # cascades will delete links, collections, and FTS via trigger?

    # Now we have all note ids, we can rebuild links and tags

def render_template(template_str, context):
    # Very simple handlebars-like
    # Supports {{var}}, {{extra.key}}, {{slug title}}, {{format-date now}}, {{format-date now "format"}}, {{filename}}, etc
    # We'll implement via regex
    def slugify(text):
        text=text.lower()
        # replace non alnum with -
        text=re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+','-',text)
        text=text.strip("-")
        return text
    def format_date(val, fmt=None):
        # val may be datetime or string "now"
        if isinstance(val, str) and val=="now":
            dt=datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        elif isinstance(val, datetime.datetime):
            dt=val
        else:
            # try parse string date
            try:
                dt=datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(val.replace("Z","+00:00"))
            except:
                dt=datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        if fmt is None:
            return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        # handle go-like format? Original uses "%Y-%m-%d" style when passed via template like "{{format-date now \"%Y-%m-%d\"}}"
        # fmt string may include %Y etc
        try:
            return dt.strftime(fmt)
        except:
            return dt.isoformat()
    # Need to handle now variable: context may have 'now' datetime
    # Handle each {{...}}
    pattern=re.compile(r'{{\s*(.*?)\s*}}')
    def repl(m):
        expr=m.group(1).strip()
        # handle slug
        if expr.startswith("slug "):
            arg=expr[5:].strip()
            val=context.get(arg, "")
            return slugify(str(val))

def eprint(s):
    sys.stderr.write(s + "\n")

def error_exit(msg):
    eprint(f"zk: error: {msg}")
    sys.exit(1)

def parse_global(argv):
    # returns notebook_dir, working_dir, no_input, help_flag, remaining (with command)
    notebook_dir=None
    working_dir=None
    no_input=False
    help_flag=False
    remaining=[]
    i=0
    while i<len(argv):
        a=argv[i]
        if a in ("-h","--help"):
            help_flag=True
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
        elif a=="--notebook-dir":
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                error_exit('expected value for --notebook-dir')
            notebook_dir=argv[i+1]
            i+=2
        elif a.startswith("--notebook-dir="):
            notebook_dir=a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a in ("-W","--working-dir"):
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                error_exit('expected value for --working-dir')
            working_dir=argv[i+1]
            i+=2
        elif a.startswith("--working-dir="):
            working_dir=a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a.startswith("-W="):
            working_dir=a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a=="--no-input":
            no_input=True
            i+=1
        elif a=="--":
            remaining.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        else:
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
    return notebook_dir, working_dir, no_input, help_flag, remaining

def find_notebook(start_dir, notebook_dir_override):
    if notebook_dir_override:
        cand = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(start_dir, notebook_dir_override)) if not os.path.isabs(notebook_dir_override) else os.path.abspath(notebook_dir_override)
        if not os.path.exists(cand):
            eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
            eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
            error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cand} or a parent directory")
        cur=cand
        while True:
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(cur, ".zk")):
                return cur
            parent=os.path.dirname(cur)
            if parent==cur:
                break
            cur=parent
        eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
        eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
        error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cand} or a parent directory")
    else:
        cur=os.path.abspath(start_dir)
        while True:
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(cur, ".zk")):
                return cur
            parent=os.path.dirname(cur)
            if parent==cur:
                break
            cur=parent
        error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {os.path.abspath(start_dir)} or a parent directory")

def load_config(notebook_dir):
    config_path=os.path.join(notebook_dir, ".zk", "config.toml")
    defaults={
        "note":{"filename":"{{id}}","extension":"md","template":"default.md","default-title":"Untitled","id-charset":"alphanum","id-length":4,"id-case":"lower"},
        "format":{"markdown":{"link-format":"wiki","hashtags":True,"colon-tags":False,"multiword-tags":False}},
        "extra":{},
        "tool":{},
    }
    try:
        try:
            import tomllib
            with open(config_path,"rb") as f:
                data=tomllib.load(f)
        except ImportError:
            import tomli
            with open(config_path,"rb") as f:
                data=tomli.load(f)
        except Exception:
            data={}
        if data:
            def deep_update(dst, src):
                for k,v in src.items():
                    if isinstance(v, dict) and k in dst and isinstance(dst[k], dict):
                        deep_update(dst[k], v)
                    else:
                        dst[k]=v
            deep_update(defaults, data)
    except Exception:
        pass
    return defaults

def parse_frontmatter(raw):
    metadata={}
    content=raw
    if raw.startswith("---\n") or raw.startswith("---\r\n"):
        lines=raw.splitlines()
        if lines and lines[0].strip()=="---":
            end_idx=-1
            for idx in range(1,len(lines)):
                if lines[idx].strip()=="---":
                    end_idx=idx
                    break
            if end_idx!=-1:
                fm_lines=lines[1:end_idx]
                for line in fm_lines:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                        continue
                    if ":" not in line:
                        continue
                    key,val=line.split(":",1)
                    key=key.strip()
                    val=val.strip()
                    if val.startswith("[") and val.endswith("]"):
                        inner=val[1:-1].strip()
                        if not inner:
                            arr=[]
                        else:
                            parts=[p.strip() for p in inner.split(",")]
                            arr=[]
                            for p in parts:
                                p=p.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
                                if p:
                                    arr.append(p)
                            val=arr
                    elif (val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"')) or (val.startswith("'") and val.endswith("'")):
                        val=val[1:-1]
                    metadata[key]=val
                content="\n".join(lines[end_idx+1:])
                if content.startswith("\n"):
                    content=content[1:]
    return metadata, content

def extract_title(metadata, content_without_fm, raw):
    if "title" in metadata and isinstance(metadata["title"], str) and metadata["title"].strip():
        return metadata["title"].strip()
    for line in content_without_fm.splitlines():
        m=re.match(r'^\s*#\s+(.*)', line)
        if m:
            t=m.group(1).strip()
            t=re.sub(r'\s+#+\s*$','',t)
            return t
    return ""

def extract_tags(metadata, body, config):
    tags=[]
    if "tags" in metadata:
        val=metadata["tags"]
        if isinstance(val, list):
            tags.extend(val)
        elif isinstance(val, str):
            if "," in val:
                tags.extend([p.strip() for p in val.split(",") if p.strip()])
            else:
                tags.extend([p.strip() for p in val.split() if p.strip()])
    hashtags_enabled=config.get("format",{}).get("markdown",{}).get("hashtags", True)
    if hashtags_enabled:
        pattern=r'(?:^|[\s])#([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)'
        for m in re.finditer(pattern, body):
            tag=m.group(1)
            if tag:
                tags.append(tag)
        colon_enabled=config.get("format",{}).get("markdown",{}).get("colon-tags", False)
        if colon_enabled:
            for m in re.finditer(r':([A-Za-z0-9_\-:]+):', body):
                tags.append(m.group(1))
    seen=set()
    uniq=[]
    for t in tags:
        if t not in seen:
            seen.add(t)
            uniq.append(t)
    return uniq

def parse_links_and_snippets(raw, paras):
    links=[]
    for para in paras:
        if not para.strip():
            continue
        snippet=para.strip()
        # wiki
        for m in re.finditer(r'\[\[([^\]]+)\]\]', para):
            inner=m.group(1)
            href=inner
            title=inner
            if "|" in inner:
                href, title = inner.split("|",1)
                href=href.strip()
                title=title.strip()
            else:
                href=href.strip()
            # remove anchor?
            href=href.split("#")[0].strip()
            try:
                start=raw.index(snippet)
            except:
                start=raw.find(para)
                if start==-1:
                    start=0
            end=start+len(snippet)
            links.append({"href": href, "title": title, "snippet": snippet, "snippet_start": start, "snippet_end": end, "type": "wiki-link", "external": 0})
        # markdown
        for m in re.finditer(r'\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]+)\)', para):
            text=m.group(1)
            href=m.group(2).strip()
            title=text if text else href
            external=1 if href.startswith("http://") or href.startswith("https://") or href.startswith("mailto:") else 0
            try:
                start=raw.index(snippet)
            except:
                start=raw.find(para)
                if start==-1:
                    start=0
            end=start+len(snippet)
            links.append({"href": href, "title": title, "snippet": snippet, "snippet_start": start, "snippet_end": end, "type": "markdown", "external": external})
    return links

def parse_note_file(notebook_dir, rel_path, config):
    abs_path=os.path.join(notebook_dir, rel_path)
    raw=open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
    checksum=hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    metadata, content_without_fm = parse_frontmatter(raw)
    title=extract_title(metadata, content_without_fm, raw)
    body_content=content_without_fm
    lines=body_content.splitlines()
    idx=0
    while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx].strip()=="":
        idx+=1
    if idx < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*#\s+', lines[idx]):
        idx+=1
        while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx].strip()=="":
            idx+=1
    body="\n".join(lines[idx:]).strip()
    if body:
        paras=[p.strip() for p in re.split(r'\n\s*\n', body) if p.strip()!='']
        lead=paras[0] if paras else ""
    else:
        paras=[]
        lead=""
    text_for_hashtags=body
    tags=extract_tags(metadata, text_for_hashtags, config)
    word_count=len(raw.split())
    links=parse_links_and_snippets(raw, paras)
    snippets=[lead] if lead else []
    filename=os.path.basename(rel_path)
    filenameStem=os.path.splitext(filename)[0]
    return {"path":rel_path,"sortable_path":rel_path,"filename":filename,"filenameStem":filenameStem,"title":title,"lead":lead,"body":body,"raw_content":raw,"word_count":word_count,"checksum":checksum,"metadata":metadata,"tags":tags,"links":links,"snippets":snippets,"paras":paras}

def index_notebook(notebook_dir, verbose=False, quiet=False, force=False):
    config=load_config(notebook_dir)
    exclude_patterns=config.get("note",{}).get("exclude",[])
    if exclude_patterns is None:
        exclude_patterns=[]
    extension=config.get("note",{}).get("extension","md")
    db_path=os.path.join(notebook_dir, ".zk", "notebook.db")
    conn=sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    cur=conn.cursor()
    all_notes=[]
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(notebook_dir):
        if ".zk" in dirs:
            dirs.remove(".zk")
        rel_root=os.path.relpath(root, notebook_dir)
        if rel_root==".":
            rel_root=""
        for fname in files:
            if not fname.endswith("."+extension):
                continue
            rel_path=os.path.join(rel_root, fname) if rel_root else fname
            rel_path=rel_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
            excluded=False
            for pat in exclude_patterns:
                if fnmatch.fnmatch(rel_path, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(fname, pat):
                    excluded=True
                    break
            if excluded:
                continue
            all_notes.append(rel_path)
    cur.execute("SELECT id, path, checksum, created, modified FROM notes")
    existing={row[1]: (row[0], row[2], row[3], row[4]) for row in cur.fetchall()}
    added=0
    modified_cnt=0
    removed=0
    seen=set()
    # detailed per file status for verbose
    status_lines=[]
    for rel_path in sorted(all_notes):
        seen.add(rel_path)
        abs_path=os.path.join(notebook_dir, rel_path)
        parsed=parse_note_file(notebook_dir, rel_path, config)
        checksum=parsed["checksum"]
        if rel_path in existing:
            nid, old_checksum, old_created, old_modified = existing[rel_path]
            if not force and checksum==old_checksum:
                status_lines.append(("- unchanged", rel_path))
                continue
            else:
                # modified
                stat=os.stat(abs_path)
                try:
                    ns=stat.st_mtime_ns
                    sec=ns//1_000_000_000
                    nsec=ns%1_000_000_000
                    dt=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(sec, tz=timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=nsec//1000)
                    db_modified=f"{dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}.{nsec:09d}+00:00"
                except:
                    dt=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(os.path.getmtime(abs_path), tz=timezone.utc)
                    db_modified=dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f+00:00")
                cur.execute("UPDATE notes SET title=?, lead=?, body=?, raw_content=?, word_count=?, checksum=?, modified=?, metadata=?, filename=?, sortable_path=? WHERE id=?",
                            (parsed["title"], parsed["lead"], parsed["body"], parsed["raw_content"], parsed["word_count"], checksum, db_modified, json.dumps(parsed["metadata"]), parsed["filename"], parsed["sortable_path"], nid))
                try:
                    cur.execute("INSERT INTO notes_fts(notes_fts, rowid, path, title, body) VALUES('delete', ?, ?, ?, ?)", (nid, parsed["path"], parsed["title"], parsed["body"]))
                    cur.execute("INSERT INTO notes_fts(rowid, path, title, body) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", (nid, parsed["path"], parsed["title"], parsed["body"]))
                except:
                    pass
                status_lines.append(("- modified", rel_path))
                modified_cnt+=1
                existing[rel_path]=(nid, checksum, old_created, db_modified)
        else:
            stat=os.stat(abs_path)
            try:
                ns=stat.st_mtime_ns
                sec=ns//1_000_000_000
                nsec=ns%1_000_000_000
                dt=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(sec, tz=timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=nsec//1000)
                db_modified=f"{dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}.{nsec:09d}+00:00"
                now_ns=time.time_ns()
                now_sec=now_ns//1_000_000_000
                now_nsec=now_ns%1_000_000_000
                now_dt=datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(now_sec, tz=timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=now_nsec//1000)
                db_created=f"{now_dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}.{now_nsec:09d}+00:00"
            except:
                now=datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc)
                db_created=now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f+00:00")
                db_modified=db_created
            cur.execute("INSERT INTO notes (path, sortable_path, title, lead, body, raw_content, word_count, checksum, created, modified, metadata, filename) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                        (parsed["path"], parsed["sortable_path"], parsed["title"], parsed["lead"], parsed["body"], parsed["raw_content"], parsed["word_count"], checksum, db_created, db_modified, json.dumps(parsed["metadata"]), parsed["filename"]))
            nid=cur.lastrowid
            try:
                cur.execute("INSERT INTO notes_fts(rowid, path, title, body) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", (nid, parsed["path"], parsed["title"], parsed["body"]))
            except:
                pass
            existing[rel_path]=(nid, checksum, db_created, db_modified)
            status_lines.append(("- added", rel_path))
            added+=1
    # deletions
    for path, (nid,_,_,_) in list(existing.items()):
        if path not in seen:
            cur.execute("DELETE FROM notes WHERE id=?", (nid,))
            try:
                cur.execute("INSERT INTO notes_fts(notes_fts, rowid, path, title, body) VALUES('delete', ?, ?, ?, ?)", (nid, path, "", ""))
            except:
                pass
            status_lines.append(("- removed", path))
            removed+=1
            del existing[path]
    # rebuild links/tags
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM links")
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM notes_collections")
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM collections")
    cur.execute("SELECT id, path FROM notes")
    path_to_id={r[1]: r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()}
    for rel_path in seen:
        # Use set may be unordered, ensure sorted for deterministic
        pass
    for rel_path in sorted(seen):
        parsed=parse_note_file(notebook_dir, rel_path, config)
        nid=path_to_id[rel_path]
        for tag in parsed["tags"]:
            cur.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO collections (kind, name) VALUES ('tag', ?)", (tag,))
            cur.execute("SELECT id FROM collections WHERE kind='tag' AND name=?", (tag,))
            cid=cur.fetchone()[0]
            cur.execute("INSERT INTO notes_collections (note_id, collection_id) VALUES (?,?)", (nid, cid))
        for link in parsed["links"]:
            href=link["href"]
            target_id=None
            target_path=None
            if href in path_to_id:
                target_id=path_to_id[href]
                target_path=href
            elif not href.endswith(".md") and href+".md" in path_to_id:
                target_id=path_to_id[href+".md"]
                target_path=href+".md"
            else:
                # stem match
                is_external=link["external"]
                if not is_external:
                    stem=os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(href))[0]
                    for p, nid2 in path_to_id.items():
                        if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0]==stem:
                            target_id=nid2
                            target_path=p
                            break
            cur.execute("INSERT INTO links (source_id, target_id, title, href, external, rels, snippet, snippet_start, snippet_end, type) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                        (nid, target_id, link["title"], link["href"], link["external"], "", link["snippet"], link["snippet_start"], link["snippet_end"], link["type"]))
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
    total=len(seen)
    # Handle verbose/quiet output inside? We'll return status for caller to print
    return {"total":total,"added":added,"modified":modified_cnt,"removed":removed,"status":status_lines}

def render_template(template_str, context):
    def slugify(text):
        text=text.lower()
        text=re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+','-',text)
        text=text.strip("-")
        return text
    def format_date(val, fmt=None):
        if isinstance(val, str) and val=="now":
            dt=context.get("_now", datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc))
        elif isinstance(val, datetime.datetime):
            dt=val
        else:
            try:
                dt=datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(str(val).replace("Z","+00:00"))
            except:
                dt=context.get("_now", datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc))
        if fmt is None:
            return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        try:
            return dt.strftime(fmt)
        except:
            return dt.isoformat()
    pattern=re.compile(r'{{\s*(.*?)\s*}}')
    def repl(m):
        expr=m.group(1).strip()
        if expr.startswith("slug "):
            arg=expr[5:].strip()
            val=context.get(arg,"")
            return slugify(str(val))
        elif expr.startswith("format-date"):
            inner=expr[len("format-date"):].strip()
            parts=re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"|\'([^\']*)\'|(\S+)', inner)
            tokens=[]
            for a,b,c in parts:
                if a:
                    tokens.append(a)
                elif b:
                    tokens.append(b)
                elif c:
                    tokens.append(c)
            if not tokens:
                return ""
            val_token=tokens[0]
            if val_token=="now":
                val="now"
            else:
                val=context.get(val_token, val_token)
            fmt=tokens[1] if len(tokens)>1 else None
            return format_date(val, fmt)
        elif expr.startswith("json "):
            return json.dumps(context)
        elif "." in expr:
            parts=expr.split(".",1)
            base, rest=parts[0], parts[1]
            if base=="extra":
                return str(context.get("extra",{}).get(rest,""))
            elif base=="metadata":
                return str(context.get("metadata",{}).get(rest,""))
            else:
                return ""
        else:
            if expr=="title-or-path":
                return context.get("title") or context.get("path") or ""
            if expr=="filename-stem":
                return context.get("filenameStem","")
            if expr=="now":
                return datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f +0000 UTC")
            return str(context.get(expr,""))
    return pattern.sub(repl, template_str)

def load_template_file(notebook_dir, template_path):
    if os.path.isabs(template_path) or template_path.startswith("~/"):
        expanded=os.path.expanduser(template_path)
        if os.path.exists(expanded):
            return open(expanded, "r", encoding="utf-8").read()
        else:
            return None
    cand=os.path.join(notebook_dir, ".zk", "templates", template_path)
    if os.path.exists(cand):
        return open(cand, "r", encoding="utf-8").read()
    cand2=os.path.join(notebook_dir, template_path)
    if os.path.exists(cand2):
        return open(cand2, "r", encoding="utf-8").read()
    return None

def parse_date_str(s):
    # Try to parse many formats: ISO, YYYY-MM-DD, relative like "today", "yesterday", "last week", "last two weeks", "2 weeks ago" ?
    s=s.strip()
    now=datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    low=s.lower()
    if low in ("today","now"):
        return now
    if low=="yesterday":
        return now - datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    if low=="tomorrow":
        return now + datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    # last X weeks
    m=re.match(r'last\s+(\d+)?\s*weeks?', low)
    if m:
        num=m.group(1)
        n=int(num) if num else 1
        return now - datetime.timedelta(weeks=n)
    m=re.match(r'last\s+two\s+weeks', low)
    if m:
        return now - datetime.timedelta(weeks=2)
    if low=="last week":
        return now - datetime.timedelta(weeks=1)
    if low=="last month":
        return now - datetime.timedelta(days=30)
    if low=="last year":
        return now - datetime.timedelta(days=365)
    # generic: try dateutil via fromisoformat and strptime
    # Try ISO with T
    try:
        # handle like 2026-09-06T14:07:32.529984522Z -> need to truncate nanoseconds to microseconds
        # Replace Z with +00:00 and truncate to 6 digits after dot
        t=s
        if t.endswith("Z"):
            t=t[:-1]+"+00:00"
        # truncate nanoseconds to microseconds (6 digits)
        m2=re.match(r'(.+\.\d{6})\d*(.*)', t)
        if m2:
            t=m2.group(1)+m2.group(2)
        dt=datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(t)
        if dt.tzinfo is None:
            dt=dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        return dt
    except:
        pass
    for fmt in ("%Y-%m-%d", "%Y/%m/%d", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", "%d/%m/%Y", "%m/%d/%Y"):
        try:
            dt=datetime.datetime.strptime(s, fmt)
            dt=dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
            return dt
        except:
            continue
    # fallback: try parse as YYYY-MM-DD without time
    try:
        dt=datetime.datetime.strptime(s[:10], "%Y-%m-%d")
        dt=dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        return dt
    except:
        pass
    # default return now
    return now

def eprint(s):
    sys.stderr.write(s + "\n")

def error_exit(msg):
    eprint(f"zk: error: {msg}")
    sys.exit(1)

def parse_global(argv):
    # returns notebook_dir, working_dir, no_input, help_flag, remaining (with command)
    notebook_dir=None
    working_dir=None
    no_input=False
    help_flag=False
    remaining=[]
    i=0
    while i<len(argv):
        a=argv[i]
        if a in ("-h","--help"):
            help_flag=True
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
        elif a=="--notebook-dir":
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                error_exit('expected value for --notebook-dir')
            notebook_dir=argv[i+1]
            i+=2
        elif a.startswith("--notebook-dir="):
            notebook_dir=a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a in ("-W","--working-dir"):
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                error_exit('expected value for --working-dir')
            working_dir=argv[i+1]
            i+=2
        elif a.startswith("--working-dir="):
            working_dir=a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a.startswith("-W="):
            working_dir=a.split("=",1)[1]
            i+=1
        elif a=="--no-input":
            no_input=True
            i+=1
        elif a=="--":
            remaining.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        else:
            remaining.append(a)
            i+=1
    return notebook_dir, working_dir, no_input, help_flag, remaining

def find_notebook(start_dir, notebook_dir_override):
    if notebook_dir_override:
        cand = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(start_dir, notebook_dir_override)) if not os.path.isabs(notebook_dir_override) else os.path.abspath(notebook_dir_override)
        if not os.path.exists(cand):
            eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
            eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
            error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cand} or a parent directory")
        cur=cand
        while True:
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(cur, ".zk")):
                return cur
            parent=os.path.dirname(cur)
            if parent==cur:
                break
            cur=parent
        eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
        eprint(f"zk: warning: lstat {cand}: no such file or directory")
        error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cand} or a parent directory")
    else:
        cur=os.path.abspath(start_dir)
        while True:
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(cur, ".zk")):
                return cur
            parent=os.path.dirname(cur)
            if parent==cur:
                break
            cur=parent
        error_exit(f"failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {os.path.abspath(start_dir)} or a parent directory")

def load_config(notebook_dir):
    config_path=os.path.join(notebook_dir, ".zk", "config.toml")
    defaults={
        "note":{"filename":"{{id}}","extension":"md","template":"default.md","default-title":"Untitled","id-charset":"alphanum","id-length":4,"id-case":"lower"},
        "format":{"markdown":{"link-format":"wiki","hashtags":True,"colon-tags":False,"multiword-tags":False}},
        "extra":{},
        "tool":{},
    }
    try:
        try:
            import tomllib
            with open(config_path,"rb") as f:
                data=tomllib.load(f)
        except ImportError:
            import tomli
            with open(config_path,"rb") as f:
                data=tomli.load(f)
        except Exception:
            data={}
        if data:
            def deep_update(dst, src):
                for k,v in src.items():
                    if isinstance(v, dict) and k in dst and isinstance(dst[k], dict):
                        deep_update(dst[k], v)
                    else:
                        dst[k]=v
            deep_update(defaults, data)
    except Exception:
        pass
    return defaults
